statements.text: Well, the upscaling of AI technology can provide censorship operations. [...] That just gives you an idea of the absolute scope of what AI can do for violating people's First Amendment rights.
statements.context: Congresswoman Harriet Hageman questions a witness at a House Weaponization of the Federal Government hearing about AI-enabled censorship.

statements.text: AI is not going to stop, and even for those of us who are concerned about it, we must move forward with AI if we are going to continue to compete with our adversaries, namely China. [...] We are truly at the outset of this developing technology, and Congress must adapt and evolve with it, not respond to what will eventually be an unfixable problem years down the road.
statements.venue: Questions for the Record, House Weaponization subcommittee hearing

statements.text: These allegations are that AI can access bank accounts and look inside those accounts, versus just seeing activities in the account.
statements.context: House Judiciary Subcommittee on the Weaponization of the Federal Government hearing, March 7, 2024.

statements.text: Also, concern with the evolution of AI in relation to this is liberty infringing regime that we're dealing with right now, the Biden Administration, is the fact that it removes human accountability. [...] Yet, with AI, that paper trail is going to disappear. Mr. Michel, what could another lawyer of secrecy achieve by displacing human action with AI do to further erode our liberties and basic guarantees of privacy?
statements.context: Question posed during a House Judiciary Committee hearing on the Weaponization of the Federal Government.

statements.text: Saying that the Chief AI Officer is ``not aware'' of the Department coordinating with the IRS to use AI to unconstitutionally spy on Americans financial records is very different from saying unequivocally that the Department is not doing so.
statements.context: House Oversight Committee hearing on the U.S. Department of Justice, where Rep. Harriet Hageman questions Attorney General Merrick Garland about DOJ's use of AI for financial surveillance.

statements.text: the DOJ was working with the IRS to use artificial intelligence to surveil bank accounts of Americans in a clearly unconstitutional manner.
statements.context: House oversight hearing for the U.S. Department of Justice, where Representative Harriet Hageman questions Attorney General Merrick Garland about alleged AI-powered financial surveillance.

statements.text: Thank you. China is trying to control the global AI sector through extensive state-directed investments, aggressive subsidies, and protectionist trade measures. It is making substantial investments to secure its global position through initiatives like Made in China 2025 and the New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan.
statements.context: Congressional hearing titled 'Artificial Intelligence: Examining Trends in Innovation and Competition,' where Rep. Harriet Hageman questions a witness.

statements.text: Now, the Artificial Intelligence Act will impose significant compliance costs on affected companies, particularly American businesses that play a pivotal role within the AI sector.
statements.context: House committee hearing on AI innovation and competition, during a question-and-answer exchange with a witness.

statements.text: I'm glad to hear that, and I'm also excited to hear about your optimism, because what would be the strategic consequences if China achieved dominance in the global AI space?
statements.context: Question posed during a House subcommittee hearing on AI innovation and competition.

statements.text: AI is advancing faster than our institutions are prepared for, and we either allow technology to become a tool for propaganda or insist it serves the truth. The FAIR Act draws that line. It demands that government-procured AI be factual and remain neutral without bending to any social or political agendas.
statements.venue: Press release on FAIR Act introduction

statements.text: Artificial intelligence is being integrated into every aspect of our society in the 21 st century, including our court systems. As an attorney for over three decades, I know our justice system demands precision and security. Congress must protect the integrity of our courts with vigorous oversight that remains up to date with emerging technologies.
statements.venue: Joint press release on AI in Courts Act

statements.text: The First Amendment does not have an AI exemption. Federal employees who pressure AI companies to filter viewpoints, distort content, or spy on users based on their beliefs will face real legal consequences. Americans deserve a way to fight back, and my Preventing AI Censorship Act gives them one.
statements.venue: Press release on Preventing AI Censorship Act

statements.text: Many are rightfully concerned about high water consumption rates by data centers in our communities where every drop of water is accounted for and needed, so I am even more concerned that this contamination seemingly came from your facility's closed-loop cooling system, a technology that is marketed as being a solution to high data center water consumption rates.
statements.venue: Letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, reported by Cowboy State Daily

statements.text: The First Amendment, however, does not have an AI exemption. Congress must be proactive to ensure Americans' right to free speech remains protected in a digital era radically transformed by the advent of AI.

Artificial intelligence is on the cusp of transforming everything, but we cannot allow the AI revolution to transform the Constitution into a mere suggestion. I am, however, still optimistic about AI's potential for humanity despite these concerns about use in courts and censorship. The AI boom may prove as transformative as the first wave of the industrial revolution, accelerating miracle advancements in medicine, engineering and manufacturing.

The rapid innovation in technology has ignited a similarly rapid increase in demand for affordable, reliable energy. Wyoming's abundant coal, oil, gas and uranium reserves hold the keys to unlocking the full potential of this digital future. I believe the wise embrace of AI will continue to steer America to rely on Wyoming energy and minerals to pioneer the 21st-century digital frontier as the nation's number one producer of coal and uranium.
